DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 127 s. 2021 13 December 2021 Dir. JUAN JOVIAN E. INGENIERO Regional Director DILG Region 6 — Western Visayas P. Aquino Street, Fort San Pedro, Iloilo City Dear Dir. Ingeniero: This refers to your Memorandum dated 28 October 2021 requesting for a legal opinion on the propriety of the following: a. Memorandum Order No. 2021-10-021 issued by Hon. Laurence Marxlen J. Dela Cruz (Mayor Dela Cruz), Mayor of Don Salvador Benedicto, Negros Occidental stating that the presentation of a COVID-19 vaccination card is an essential requirement for the renewal of appointment of a Job Order personnel; and b. The "No Vaccine, No Entry" Policy in government buildings adopted by multiple local government units in the region. For guidance, Memorandum Order No. 2021-10-021 states as follows: "In line with our continual compliance with the Minimum Public Health Standard of the Inter- Agency Task Force (IATF) for the Management of Emerging Infectious Diseases, you are all advised to have yourself vaccinated against COVID-19 and present your vaccination card before my office as essential requirement for your renewal of appointment." This Department is of the opinion that: (a) the local government unit (LGU) may require job order workers to present their vaccination cards as a pre-requisite for their initial or renewal of contracts; and (b) the local government units may not require individuals to present a vaccination card to transact with the government. "No Vaccine, No Renewal" Policy for Job Order Workers First and foremost, a Job Order (JO) is defined under Civil Service Commission (CSC) — Commission on Audit (COA), and Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Joint Circular No. I, series of 2017 (the Joint Circular) as: "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.. 8876-34-54

"5.4. Job Order refers to piece work (pakyaw) or intermittent or emergency jobs such as clearing of debris on the roads, canals, waterways, etc. after natural/ man-made disasters/occurrences, and other manual/trades and crafts services such as carpentry, plumbing, electrical, and the like. These jobs are of short duration and for a specific piece of work. The same Joint Circular states that workers engaged through a Job Order are not considered as employees, and are not covered by CSC Rules and Regulations. Additionally, their service, regardless of the length thereof, shall not be interpreted as years in government service. JO workers are, therefore, akin to 'consultants' whose engagements are primarily dictated by the terms and conditions set in their contract and in accordance with the provisions of Republic Act No. 386, otherwise known as the New Civil Code of the Philippines. Meanwhile, this Department confirms that LGUs are authorized by the Local Government Code to engage the services of JO workers, to wit: Section 77. Responsibility for Human Resources and Development. - The chief executive of every local government unit shall be responsible for human resources and development in his unit and shall take all personnel actions in accordance with the Constitutional provisions on civil service, pertinent laws, and rules and regulations thereon, including such policies, guidelines and standards as the Civil Service Commission may establish: Provided, That the local chief executive may employ emergency or casual employees or laborers paid on a daily wage or piecework basis and hired through job orders for local projects authorized by the sanggunian concemed, without need of approval or attestation by the Civil Service Commission: Provided, further, That the period of employment of emergency or casual laborers as provided in this Section shall not exceed six (6) months. 1 Section 76. Organizational Structure and Staffing Pattern. — Every local government unit shall design and implement its own organizational structure and staffing pattern taking into consideration its service requirements and financial capability, subject to the minimum standards and guidelines prescribed by the Civil Service Commission. Verily, local chief executives, such as the mayor of a municipality, may engage daily- paid and/or piece-rate persons as JO workers. Their contracts do not need the approval or attestation by the CSC, but must still comply with the minimum standards set forth by the same. In 2017, the Civil Service Commission, together with the Commission on Audit (COA) and the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) issued CSC-COA-DBM Joint Circular No. 1, series of 2017 (CSC-COA-DBM JC 1-2017) entitled "Rules and Regulations Governing Contract of Service and Job Order Workers in the Government", which states: 6.3. Job Order Government agencies may hire JO workers subject to the following conditions: 6.3. I The services of a JO worker is either paid according to an agreed contract amount for the piece of work or on a daily wage basis. Emphasis supplied. Page 2 of 4

6.3.2 Contracting the services of JO workers shall be subject to pertinent budgeting, accounting, and auditing rules and regulations. 7.0. Limitations 7.2. Hiring of JO workers shall be limited to emergency or intermittent work, such as clearing of debris on the roads, canals, waterways, etc. after natural/ manmade disasters/occurrences; other trades and crafts, and manual tasks such as carpentry, plumbing, painting, electrical, and the like which are not part of the regular functions of the agency. 7.3 COS and JO workers should not, in any case, be made to perform functions which are part of the job description of the agency's existing regular employees. 7.4 COS and JO workers should not be designated to positions exercising control or supervision over regular and career employees. 7.5 The services of the COS and JO workers are not covered by Civil Service laws, rules, and regulations, thus, not creditable as government service. They do not enjoy the benefits being received by government employees, such as leave, Personnel Economic Relief Allowance, Representation and Transportation Allowances, and Other bonuses and incentives. The regulations set by CSC-COA-DBM JC 1-2017 do not prohibit LGUs from requiring JOS to undergo health screening and/or vaccinations. Absent an existing law, the authority to determine the standards of hiring JOS lies within an LGU's discretion pursuant to the principle of local autonomy. In view thereof, an LGU may include in its criteria for hiring and renewal of JOS that the latter be vaccinated from COVID-19. Verily, this Department is of the opinion that Mayor Dela Cruz may require JOS to present their COVID-19 vaccination cards as a pre-requisite for the renewal of their contracts. Memorandum Order No. 2021-10-021 issued by the Office of the Mayor of Don Salvador Benedicto, Negros Occidental is valid. "No Vaccine, No Entry" Policy in LGU Buildings We shall now delve into the validity ofvarious LGUs' "No Vaccination, No Entry" Policy. Based on the Memorandum of Dir. Ingeniero, a number of LGUs are requiring individual to present their vaccination cards as a pre-requisite to enter government buildings. Republic Act No. 11525, otherwise known as the "COVID-19 Vaccination Program of 2021" states as follows: Section 12 COVID-19 Vaccine Card — xxxx The issuance of a vaccine card is intended to be digital, but shall remain accessible through other means such as printed cards... Provided further, That the vaccine cards shall not be considered as an additional mandatory requirement for educational, employment and other similar government transaction purposes... xxxx Verily, the government, including the LGUs, may not require individuals to present their vaccination cards as a pre-requisite to transact with the government. This level further notes that the 'No Vaccine, No Entry' Policy imposed in government buildings Page 3 of 4

may be deemed as a curtailment of the RA 1 1525, as it is reasonable to assume that persons entering government buildings are there to transact or engage with the government. As such, this Department concurs with your opinion that the 'No Vaccine, No Entry' Policy imposed by LGUs on government establishments is invalid. This Department notes, however, that LGUs with adequate vaccine supply may impose reasonable alternatives for persons who are still unvaccinated. The local sanggunian may instead issue an ordinance requiring individuals to present either a vaccination card, or a negative COVID-19 test as a pre-requisite to enter government buildings. Such regulation does not violate RA 11525, and is in line with the General Welfare Clause2 of the Local Government Code, which provides: "Section 16. General Welfare. - Every local government unit shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Within their respective territorial jurisdictions, local government units shall ensure and support, among other things, the preservation and enrichment of culture, promote health and safety, enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology, encourage and support the development of appropriate and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, improve public morals, enhance economic prosperity and social justice, promote full employment among their residents, maintain peace and order, and preserve the comfort and convenience of their inhabitants." This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: INGAN Unders retary for Local Government ousLG/MLl/LLLS-LRALLD/kuq 2 Section 16, Local Government Code. Page 4 of 4
